profile.reading:
Per CoreSite's own facility page, this building, VA1, is located at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive, Reston, VA 20191, part of CoreSite's three-building Reston campus alongside VA2 and VA3. CoreSite publishes 261,000-plus square feet for VA1 on the main facility page; the operator's spec-sheet landing page instead cites a forward-looking campus total of "more than 1.3 million square feet of colocation space upon full build out," and the VA1 page separately describes the three-building campus as totaling "over 986,000 square feet" today, two different campus-wide figures that do not reconcile with each other. No MW capacity or opening year is stated for VA1 specifically; the operator cites N+2 generator redundancy for the campus. CoreSite lists SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA compliance for its facilities generally.

Virginia's data center boom is reshaping statewide electricity rates directly relevant to this Reston campus. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved new Dominion Energy rates raising a typical residential bill by about $16 a month to roughly $165, while creating a new GS-5 rate class for data centers effective January 1, 2027, under which facilities with 25 megawatts or more of demand face 14-year mandatory contracts and minimum cost-coverage requirements, per Inside Climate News.

American Tower reported record leasing at CoreSite driving stronger-than-expected second-quarter 2026 results, projecting data-center segment revenue of $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026, roughly 14.9% growth at the midpoint, and raising its full-year outlook on the strength of that performance; the company also budgeted approximately $695 million in data-center development spending for 2026, funding continued build-out across the Reston campus among CoreSite's other markets.

reading.body:
CoreSite VA1 is a 261,000-square-foot building at 12100 Sunrise Valley Drive in Reston, part of a three-building campus that CoreSite describes as totaling over 986,000 square feet today with potential expansion to 1.3 million square feet. The operator publishes no megawatt capacity figure for VA1 specifically, making it impossible to assess the building's contribution to Virginia's data center load or its relevance to AI infrastructure scaling. The facility holds SOC 1 Type 2, SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, NIST 800-53, PCI DSS, and HIPAA certifications, qualifying it to host regulated enterprise and financial workloads. CoreSite operates the campus with N+2 generator redundancy.

Virginia's regulatory environment is shifting the economics of data center siting at this location. In November 2026, the Virginia State Corporation Commission approved a new Dominion Energy rate class effective January 1, 2027, requiring facilities drawing 25 megawatts or more to sign 14-year contracts with minimum cost-coverage requirements. This regulatory change directly affects any tenant at VA1 planning sustained AI compute operations at scale, since such deployments typically demand power levels that would trigger the new mandatory long-term contracting regime.

American Tower, which acquired CoreSite in 2021 and now operates this campus, reported record leasing activity driving stronger-than-expected results in the second quarter of 2026, with data-center segment revenue projected at $1.20 billion to $1.22 billion for full-year 2026 and $695 million budgeted for continued data-center development across the Reston campus in 2026. Without a published power figure for VA1, the campus ranks 24th among Virginia's 23 facilities with disclosed megawatt capacity, indicating it likely exceeds published peers in absolute terms but remains unmeasured by the operator's own disclosure.
